node_hits.rationale: Walkthrough covers the full monthly close sequence: sub-ledger close for AP/AR, manual accrual journals, account reconciliations with dual-review sign-off, trial balance lock, and handoff to consolidation. Accruals explicitly called out as manual pain point.

evidence.quote: Close starts on business day one. We run the sub-ledger close for AP and AR first, then post accruals manually in the GL. Most of the accrual entries are keyed by hand into the ERP.
evidence.note: Close sequence: sub-ledger (AP/AR) then manual accruals in ERP.

evidence.quote: accruals are fully manual today. The team builds them in spreadsheets and re-keys them. It's a real pain point every month and the most common source of late adjustments.
evidence.note: Accruals fully manual — spreadsheets then re-keyed; identified as primary pain point and source of late adjustments.

evidence.quote: After the trial balance is locked we move to account reconciliations. Each balance sheet account owner signs off in our recon tool, but the sign-off is decentralized — every regional controller owns their own accounts.
evidence.note: Account reconciliations decentralized by regional controller.

evidence.quote: Once recons are signed off, we hand the consolidated trial balance to the consolidation team for eliminations and topside entries.
evidence.note: Handoff to consolidation for eliminations and topside entries.

evidence.quote: Let's keep going with management review.
evidence.note: Management review mentioned as next step in close.

lens_signals.rationale: Accruals explicitly called 'a real pain point every month' and cited as the most common source of late adjustments.
Accrual journals are fully manual: built in spreadsheets and re-keyed into the ERP with no automation.
Account reconciliation sign-off is decentralized — every regional controller owns their own accounts.

candidate_findings.observation: Accruals are fully manual: built in spreadsheets and re-keyed into the ERP every month. Identified by the controller as the primary pain point and most common source of late adjustments.
candidate_findings.recommended_action: Evaluate automated accrual journal upload or ERP-native accrual workflow to eliminate spreadsheet re-keying.

candidate_findings.observation: Reconciliation sign-off is decentralized across regional controllers with no central oversight structure described.

node_hits.rationale: A dual-review control requiring second-level approval for all reconciliations above $50K is described as operating every close. However, it is stated verbally by the controller and is not documented in any policy or system configuration.

evidence.quote: we require a second-level reviewer to approve every reconciliation above fifty thousand dollars before the account is closed. That dual-review control is enforced every single close.
evidence.note: Dual-review control claimed to operate every close — stated verbally by controller.

evidence.quote: Honestly, no. It's how we've always done it but it isn't written into any policy or system config. It lives in people's heads.
evidence.note: Dual-review control is NOT documented in policy or system configuration — tribal knowledge.

lens_signals.rationale: Controller asserts dual-review operates every close, though only verbal evidence.
Control relies on undocumented tribal knowledge rather than policy or system enforcement — a process risk.

candidate_findings.observation: The dual-review control for reconciliations >$50K is not written into any policy document or system configuration. It exists only as tribal knowledge, creating control fragility and audit risk.
candidate_findings.recommended_action: Document the dual-review threshold and approval requirement in a formal controls policy and configure the recon tool to enforce the $50K threshold systematically.
